sources: Authored in-house for three.ws on 2026-11-16. The passages are the ones in data/evals/embeddings/v1.json (same licence and provenance), regrouped here into candidate lists with hard distractors.
notes: Each item gives a query and a candidate list in which exactly one passage is relevant (index `relevant`) and the rest are hard distractors. Quality is top-1 accuracy; format adherence is the share of responses that return a full permutation of the candidates.

items.query: how do I make a still character model poseable without painting weights
passages: A static mesh exported without a skeleton can still be lit, textured and rendered, but it cannot bend at the joints.
Blendshapes can also be keyed by hand in an animation tool, which gives an artist full control over every expression.
Auto-rigging adds a humanoid skeleton and skin weights to a static mesh so it can be posed and animated without manual weight painting.
Increasing the polygon count of a model makes curved surfaces look smoother when the camera is close.

items.query: what is inside a single-file binary glTF
passages: A glTF file can reference external PNG textures and a separate .bin buffer, which is convenient when editing assets by hand.
GLB is the binary container for glTF: the JSON scene description, the vertex buffers and the textures are packed into one file.
Exporting a scene to a single flattened file is simpler to share but loses the ability to override individual layers later.
OpenUSD describes a scene as layers that can be composed and overridden, which lets several tools edit the same stage without overwriting each other.

items.query: make the avatar's lips follow the audio automatically
passages: Speech recognition converts spoken audio into text so a voice command can be handled like a typed message.

Text-to-speech turns written text into audio; multilingual voices let one avatar speak several languages with the same identity.
Audio-driven facial animation predicts blendshape weights from speech so an avatar's mouth moves in time with the voice.

items.query: wallet where the service keeps the keys for me
passages: A custodial wallet is held by the platform on the user's behalf, so the user does not manage a seed phrase themselves.
Hardware wallets keep private keys on a separate device and require a physical button press to approve each transaction.

items.query: what to do when the free model API says too many requests
passages: A 404 response means the requested resource does not exist, so retrying the same request will not help.

items.query: why can't I mix vectors from different embedding models
passages: Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors and ignores their length, which suits normalised embeddings.
Keyword search ranks documents by how often the query terms appear, which misses passages that use different words for the same idea.
A cross-encoder reranker reads the query and each candidate passage together and re-scores the top results so the most relevant context comes first.
Embedding vectors from two different models live in different spaces and cannot be compared, so stored vectors are tagged with the model that produced them.
